To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the VD-type and HWR-type 2.45 GHz rectennas have VD and HWR behavior, respectively, even without the presence of a charge pump capacitor; (2) the VD-rectenna shows a drastic improvement of the RF-to-DC conversion efficiency in comparison to the HWR-rectenna; (3) the improvement of the efficiency is caused by voltage conservation in the diodes; and (4) the improvement of RF-to-DC efficiency
the VD-type 2.45 GHz rectenna shows a higher RF-to-DC conversion efficiency compared with the HWR-type 2.4 GHz rectenna at output load greater than 100 Ω.

the VD-type RF–dc converter has a better RF–dc conversion performance than the conventional HWR-type RF–dc converters at high output loads, which was found to be caused by the voltage doubling effect in the rectenna equivalent circuits, and that this effect is attributable to the voltage conservation in a Schottky diode.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a rectenna with improved RF–dc conversion characteristics.
the analysis of the VD behavior of a 0.5- $\times $ -2.45-GHZ rectenna.
the development of an RF–dc conversion circuit that is suitable for use in rectennas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developed VD- and the conventional VD-type rectennas have the same VD behavior.
the developed VD rectenna is a new type of VD, which is different from a conventional VD.
the VD-type diode rectenna has an inherent VD behavior and shows a drastic improvement in RF–dc conversion efficiencies in comparison with the HWR-type diode rectennas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VD-type diode rectenna has a higher RF–dc conversion rate than the HWR-type diode rectennas, especially at higher output loads.
the VD-type and HWR-type VDs are the same in the sense that both of them are VDs, even though the VD-type VD does not have a charge pump capacitor.
the developed VD- and conventional VDs are not fundamentally different, and that the developed VDs can be used in the rectenna application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a VD-type rectifier with a series diode can improve the RF–dc power conversion efficiency of a rectenna, especially at high output loads.
VD-type rectennas are useful for high-power rectenna applications.
a rectenna can be designed to behave as a VD, and the rectenna can conserve dc voltage when the input microwave period is comparable to the electric discharge time constants.
